target_customer: K-12 schools and districts, starting with California and Oregon independent study, charter and personalized learning programs
problem: Legacy student information systems store records but leave schools to bolt on dozens of tools for attendance, enrollment and compliance. Scout automates that busywork, including audit packets and state reporting.
business_model: B2B SaaS per school or district (pricing not public)

founders.name: Noah Fichter
education: University of Maryland, CS degree and education policy degree
previous_startups: Sneaker-bot license seller started at age 17 (outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page: first engineer at Slash for three years.

founders.name: Max Bertfield
founders.background_notes: YC page: led a product and engineering team at TodayTix for four years and was an early engineer at several startups.

competitors.name: PowerSchool
competitors.what: Dominant K-12 SIS vendor adding an AI assistant (PowerBuddy)
competitors.traction_then: PowerBuddy rolled out across the 2024 to 2025 school year
competitors.funding_then: Public company (acquired in a take-private in 2024, per general reporting not verified here)

technical_complexity.rationale: A system of record with attendance, grading, enrollment and state compliance reporting is broad CRUD plus per-state compliance logic; the AI automation layer adds moderate difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Once a school runs its records on an SIS, switching is costly, and state specific compliance reporting (California independent study audits) is a barrier; the early product has few named customers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: PowerSchool shipped PowerBuddy AI assistants in 2024 to 2025, but they sit on top of the legacy SIS rather than replacing it.

market_need_then: Schools layer many tools on a legacy SIS and juggle annual compliance reports, according to the YC page. The company says it targets California and Oregon independent study programs where attendance and work sample audits are heavy.

branding.domain_note: Uses scoutforschools.com since the plain scout.com name belongs to others.

identity.logo: Not described in any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and mission driven; 'Onboard a student in 4 minutes, not 4 weeks' and 'For the love of learning'.

branding.brand_signature: Onboard a student in 4 minutes, not 4 weeks

brand_strength.rationale: Clear tagline and school testimonials on the site, but no press on the brand and many unrelated companies called Scout appear in search.

outcome_analysis: Scout is an active Winter 2025 company serving California and Oregon independent study schools, with named school testimonials on its site. No acquisition or shutdown news was found, and a software engineer job post suggests it was hiring. Incumbent PowerSchool added AI assistants on top of its SIS rather than replacing it, which leaves room for an AI-native system of record. Funding beyond the YC deal is not publicly confirmed.
notes: Funding sources conflict: one profile says about $500K at seed with Noah Fichter as investor, another says pre-seed in March 2025, and Crunchbase shows pre-seed with no amount. None is primary, so no round is recorded. The site says it is backed by three unnamed 'education investors'. Other companies named Scout (defense AI, Charleston workflow) are unrelated. The PowerSchool take-private is general knowledge and was not checked in a cited source, so it is not relied on. Alma is a newer SIS marketed against PowerSchool but its source page is undated, so it is not listed as a competitor at founding. The earlier statements above that no round was recorded are superseded by the completeness pass: the roughly 500K round of March 2025 rests on a single database profile (stage and amount differ between profiles; Crunchbase gives no amount). The YC page names Reach Capital and Rethink Education as investors, which no source ties to a round. Other companies named Scout (health diagnostics, YC W22) are different, not recorded.
